title: The organizational (business) market
summary: The business market covers all organizations that buy goods and services to make or supply other products. Industrial goods fall into materials and parts, capital items, and supplies and services.

chunks.heading: What is the organizational market?
chunks.explanation_md:
The **organizational market** consists of all the organizations that **acquire goods and services used in the production of other products or services** that are sold, rented or supplied to others.

It goes by several names: **B2B marketing, industrial marketing, organizational marketing, business-to-business marketing**.

Business organizations include manufacturing companies, government undertakings, private sector organizations, educational institutions, hospitals, distributors and dealers.

chunks.heading: Types of industrial products and services
chunks.explanation_md:
Industrial products and services fall into three groups:

| Group | What it is | Types and examples |
|---|---|---|
| **Materials and parts** | Goods that enter the final product | Raw materials (iron ore, crude oil, fish, fruits, vegetables); manufactured materials (acids, fuel oil, steel, chemicals); component parts (bearings, TV tubes, small motors, batteries, tyres); subassemblies (exhaust pipe in motorcycle) |
| **Capital items** | Goods used in the production process | Light equipment or accessories (hand tools, dies, jigs, computer terminals); installations or heavy equipment (furnaces, machines, turbines); plant and building (offices, plants, warehouses, parking lots, housing) |
| **Supplies and services** | Goods and services that support the operations | Supplies (fasteners, fuels, packaging materials, lubricants, paints, electrical items); services (legal, auditing, advertising, courier, marketing research) |

chunks.heading: Business and consumer customers: Havells Fans
chunks.explanation_md:
The slide splits the market for **Havells Fans** into **B2C** and **B2B**.

- **B2C**: individuals and household customers.
- **B2B** has three customer types: **commercial enterprises** (large factories; micro, small and medium organisations), **government customers** (central government undertakings, state government firms) and **institutional customers** (hospitals, schools and colleges, hotels).

questions.model_answer_md:
1. **Materials and parts**, which enter the final product: for example raw materials such as iron ore, or component parts such as batteries.

questions.stem: Using Havells Fans, explain the consumer and business markets.
questions.model_answer_md:
Havells Fans serves two markets:

- **B2C**: individuals and household customers.
- **B2B** with three customer types: **commercial enterprises** (large factories, micro, small and medium organisations), **government customers** (central government undertakings, state government firms) and **institutional customers** (hospitals, schools and colleges, hotels).

questions.stem: Explain the organizational market and the types of industrial products and services.
questions.model_answer_md:
The **organizational market** (B2B, industrial or business-to-business marketing) consists of organizations that acquire goods and services used in the production of other products or services that are sold, rented or supplied to others. Buyers include manufacturing companies, government undertakings, educational institutions, hospitals, distributors and dealers.

Industrial products and services have three groups:

**Materials and parts** (enter the final product): raw materials (iron ore, crude oil), manufactured materials (steel, chemicals), component parts (bearings, batteries, tyres) and subassemblies (exhaust pipe in motorcycle).

**Capital items** (used in production): light equipment (hand tools, dies), installations or heavy equipment (furnaces, machines, turbines), plant and building (offices, warehouses).

**Supplies and services** (support operations): supplies such as fasteners, fuels and paints, and services such as legal, auditing, advertising, courier and marketing research.

The Havells Fans example splits customers into B2C and B2B (commercial, government, institutional).

**Conclusion.** What defines the market is that buyers use the goods to produce or supply other things.
